Dynamic noise after orbital tuning (DYNOT)

Source: R/dynot.R
dynot.Rd

The dynot function runs the DYNOT sedimentary noise model of Li et al. (2018a,b) on an (orbitally tuned, usually unevenly sampled) time series. In each Monte Carlo realisation a sampling interval is drawn from a Weibull distribution fitted (maximum likelihood) to the sampling intervals of the data (values outside [sample_min, sample_max] are replaced by one shared uniform draw for all low values and one for all high values, as in Acycle), a window length is drawn uniformly from [window_min, window_max], a time-bandwidth product from nw_min + k/2 and, for each target orbital frequency f, the lower and upper band limits are f -/+ fz * nw / window with fz uniform in [fz_min, fz_max]. The series is pchip-interpolated at the drawn sampling interval, linearly detrended, padded by half a window (pad_type) and analysed with the legacy power decomposition (pdan.m, see pda_legacy). The power-ratio curves are interpolated onto a regular grid, rescaled by (grand mean / realisation mean) of the power ratio, normalised to a maximum of 1 if needed, and summarized by percentiles (median plus the selected confidence intervals). The noise is 1 - power ratio. Translated from Acycle v3.1 DYNOS.m (runDynot, loadDataReady, sanitizeData), dynotIterationWorker.m, dynotPercentilePlan.m, pdan.m and zeropad2.m (Mingsong Li).

Usage

dynot(
  data = NULL,
  target_periods = c(405.6912, 130.6979, 123.8532, 98.8517, 94.8856, 40.9897, 23.682,
    22.3758, 18.9519),
  window_min = 300,
  window_max = 500,
  nw_min = 2,
  nw_max = 2,
  pad = 1000,
  step = 5,
  n_out = 1000,
  pad_type = 1,
  fz_min = 0.9,
  fz_max = 1.2,
  f_min = 0.001,
  f_max = 1,
  sample_min = NULL,
  sample_max = NULL,
  intervals = c(50, 68, 80, 90, 95),
  n_sim = 1000,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  genplot = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Tuned time series (matrix or data frame, numeric: time in column 1, e.g. in kyr, proxy value in column 2; further columns are ignored; at least 10 rows; may be unevenly sampled). Rows are sorted, duplicated times are averaged and non-finite rows removed. Required (Default=NULL).

target_periods

Periods of the target orbital cycles, in the time unit of data (numeric vector, > 0). The power within a band around each target frequency 1 / period is summed into the target power. Default=c(405.6912, 130.6979, 123.8532, 98.8517, 94.8856, 40.9897, 23.6820, 22.3758, 18.9519) (the nine Acycle default periods in kyr).

window_min, window_max

Range of the sliding window length, in the time unit of data (numeric, > 0, window_min <= window_max); each Monte Carlo realisation draws its window length uniformly from this range. Default=300 and Default=500.

nw_min

Smallest time-bandwidth product of the multitaper spectra (numeric, >= 0.5). Each realisation uses nw_min + k/2, with k drawn from 1:(2*(nw_max-nw_min)), or nw_min itself when nw_max=nw_min. Default=2.

nw_max

Largest time-bandwidth product (numeric, >= nw_min); 2*(nw_max-nw_min) must be an integer. If equal to nw_min, all realisations use nw_min. Default=2.

pad

Number of points (zero-padded FFT length) of each multitaper spectrum (integer, > 0); larger values give a finer frequency grid. Default=1000.

step

Step between successive windows of the power decomposition, in samples of the interpolated series (integer, >= 1). Default=5.

n_out

Number of points of the regular output time grid onto which the noise curves are interpolated (integer, >= 1). Default=1000.

pad_type

How the series is extended by half a window at both ends before the analysis (numeric code): 0 no padding, 1 zeros, 2 mirrored data, 3 the mean of the end segment, 4 random normal values with the mean and standard deviation of the end segment. Default=1.

fz_min, fz_max

Range of the bandwidth multiplier (numeric, > 0, fz_min <= fz_max): the lower and upper limits of each target band are f -/+ fz * nw / window, with fz drawn uniformly from this range for each limit and realisation. Default=0.9 and Default=1.2.

f_min

Lower frequency limit, in cycles per time unit (numeric, >= 0): target band limits below it are clipped to it and it is the lower edge of the total band used as denominator of the power ratio. Default=0.001.

f_max

Upper frequency limit, in cycles per time unit (numeric, > f_min): target band limits above it are clipped and it is the upper edge of the total band (itself clipped to the Nyquist frequency). Default=1.

sample_min

Smallest simulated sampling interval, in the time unit (numeric, > 0, or NULL). Each realisation interpolates the series to a sampling interval drawn from a Weibull distribution fitted to the sampling intervals of data; draws below sample_min are replaced by one shared uniform draw from [sample_min, sample_max]. NULL uses the 5th percentile of the data sampling intervals. Default=NULL.

sample_max

Largest simulated sampling interval (numeric, >= sample_min, or NULL); draws above it are replaced in the same way. NULL uses the 95th percentile of the data sampling intervals. Default=NULL.

intervals

Confidence intervals of the noise to report, in percent (numeric vector, any subset of 50, 68, 80, 90, 95); the median is always reported. Default=c(50, 68, 80, 90, 95).

n_sim

Number of Monte Carlo realisations (integer, >= 1). Default=1000.

seed

Seed of the random number generator (integer), so that the Monte Carlo results can be reproduced; NULL leaves the current random state unchanged. Default=NULL.

verbose

Show a progress bar over the realisations (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

genplot

Plot the result with plot_dynot (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

Value

A list with elements percentile: matrix [time, noise percentiles] on the grid points where the median is defined (column names give the percentile levels); median: matrix [time, median noise]; percentiles: percentile levels; median_index; interval_count: number of confidence intervals; grid: full output grid; noise: matrix (n_out x n_sim) of adjusted noise (1 - adjusted power ratio) of every realisation; power_mean: mean power ratio of every realisation; draws: list with the simulated sampling intervals, windows, nw, band limits (matrix f3m) and the underlying uniform draws; weibull: fitted Weibull scale and shape; sample_range; data: the cleaned input data.

References

Li, M., Hinnov, L.A., Huang, C., Ogg, J.G., 2018a. Sedimentary noise and sea levels linked to land-ocean water exchange and obliquity forcing. Nature Communications 9, 1004. doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03454-y

Li, M., Huang, C., Hinnov, L., Chen, W., Ogg, J., Tian, W., 2018b. Astrochronology of the Anisian stage (Middle Triassic) at the Guandao reference section, South China. Earth and Planetary Science Letters 482, 591-606. doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2017.11.042

Li, M., Huang, C., Hinnov, L., Ogg, J., Chen, Z.-Q., Zhang, Y., 2016. Obliquity-forced climate during the Early Triassic hothouse in China. Geology 44, 623-626. doi:10.1130/G37970.1

Author

Michiel Arts (R translation); original MATLAB code: Mingsong Li (Acycle).

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(2)
t <- cumsum(runif(900, 1, 3))
x <- sin(2 * pi * t / 405) + sin(2 * pi * t / 100) +
  sin(2 * pi * t / 41) + rnorm(900) * (0.2 + t / max(t))
res <- dynot(data = cbind(t, x), n_sim = 20, n_out = 200, seed = 1)
plot_dynot(res)

# }
